hard_questions.question: Select the clause structure: 'Sing repeatedly that verse'.
hard_questions.answer: PAC (Predicator-Adjunct-Complement) [64]

hard_questions.question: Identify the function of the underlined part: 'Adeyemi, **the cobbler**, was arrested'.
hard_questions.answer: Appositive element to 'Adeyemi' [83, 84]

hard_questions.question: What is the difference between a 'root' and a 'stem'?
hard_questions.answer: Root is the core meaningful part; stem is the part remaining after removing inflectional affixes [31, 85]

hard_questions.question: Identify the function of 'that Nigeria is rich' in: 'The notion that Nigeria is rich may not be correct'.
hard_questions.answer: Noun clause, appositive element to 'The notion' [66, 86]

hard_questions.question: Select the clause structure: 'Ola loves the man deeply'.
hard_questions.answer: SPCA (Subject-Predicator-Complement-Adjunct) [87, 88]

hard_questions.question: State the function: 'To succeed in life is **our goal**'.
hard_questions.answer: Noun phrase, subject complement [87, 89]

hard_questions.question: Indicate the structure type: 'During a public lecture..., Apeke displayed her wealth of knowledge...'.
hard_questions.answer: Complex sentence [90]

hard_questions.question: Identify the grammatical name and function: '**Embittered by the years of neglect**, Roseline wept'.
hard_questions.answer: Participial phrase, qualifying the subject 'Roseline' [91, 92]

hard_questions.question: What are the rules for transforming an active sentence to passive?
hard_questions.answer: Subject/Object reversal, adding 'BE' verb of same tense, adding 'by' before new object [93]

hard_questions.question: Identify the function: 'I know **that you are serious**'.
hard_questions.answer: Noun clause, object of the verb [48, 69]

hard_questions.question: What is the APA 7th edition rule for citing three or more authors in subsequent text?
hard_questions.answer: First author followed by 'et al.' and year (e.g., Oshiluyi et al., 2024) [94]

hard_questions.question: Identify the name and function: 'He has been learning **swimming in the icy sea**'.
hard_questions.answer: Gerundive phrase, object of the verb phrase 'has been learning' [83, 95]

hard_questions.question: State the function: 'Going **by your comments**, we are sure of victory'.
hard_questions.answer: Adjectival function modifying 'we' [48, 96]

hard_questions.question: Identify the structure: 'Love covers **all sins**'.
hard_questions.answer: Noun phrase, object complement (per specific test marking) [61, 97]

hard_questions.question: Explain the difference between 'Anaphoric' and 'Cataphoric' references.
hard_questions.answer: Anaphoric refers backward to an antecedent; Cataphoric refers forward to a following referent [98]

hard_questions.question: Analyze the morphemes in 'individualistic'.
hard_questions.answer: individual (root) + ist (derivational) + ic (derivational) [68, 99]

hard_questions.question: Identify the function: '**If the matter is resolved on time**, there will not be unrest'.
hard_questions.answer: Adverbial clause of condition, qualifying the verb phrase 'will not be' [88, 100]

hard_questions.question: What is a 'Pseudo Cleft' sentence?
hard_questions.answer: A reversal of a wh-cleft (e.g., 'A bar of chocolate is what I would like') [101]

hard_questions.question: Identify the name and function: '**The man that stole your car** was caught'.
hard_questions.answer: Noun phrase, subject of the verb phrase 'was caught' [102, 103]

hard_questions.question: State the rules for summary writing.
hard_questions.answer: No fragments (complete sentences), avoid mindless lifting, and maintain brevity [104, 105]

hard_questions.question: Contrast the 'Frustration', 'Instructional', and 'Independent' levels of comprehension.
hard_questions.answer: Frustration: cannot comprehend; Instructional: needs help; Independent: succeeds alone [106, 107]
